summary: Takanori Unno is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his doctorate from Nagoya University, studying under Yoshifumi Ueda, Hakuju Ui, and others. He held posts at Nagoya University, Aichi Prefectural University of Fine Arts and Music, and Meijo University.

Takao Hayashi specializes in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Tohoku and Kyoto universities, and completed his PhD at Brown University under David Pingree. He held posts at Kyoto Women's University and served as assistant professor and professor at Doshisha University.
Takao Kagawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Susumu Yamaguchi, Issai Funahashi, and Shoju Inaba. He served as a professor at Bukkyo University.

Takao Maruyama is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University. He held faculty positions at Rissho University, Shinshu University (serving as professor and later emeritus professor), and Mejiro University.

Takao Moriyasu was a scholar of Iranian/Central Asian studies, history/archaeology, and Sinology. Educated at the University of Tokyo and Osaka University, he served as associate professor at Kanazawa University, professor at Osaka University, and professor at Kindai University.

Takao Yamagata was a religious studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University. He held positions at Miyagi Gakuin Women's University and served as president of the Japanese Association for the Study of Indian Religions.

Takashi Iwata is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who studied at Waseda University and earned a doctorate at the University of Hamburg under scholars including Albrecht Wezler. He served as associate professor and professor at Waseda University.
Takashi Maeda is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University. He later held teaching posts as a lecturer at Taisho University.

Takashi Nakao was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Rissho University and the Tokyo University of Education, and served as associate professor at Bunkyo University Women's College and professor at Rissho University.

Takashi Ogawa specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Komazawa University, Peking University, and the University of Tokyo, and served as an associate professor at Komazawa University.
Takashi Yamada is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who studied at Hosei University. He served as an associate professor at the Prefectural University of Kumamoto.
Takatoshi Ito is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Komazawa University.
Takatoshi Nakamura is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ryukai Mano. He served as a researcher at the Comprehensive Buddhist Studies Institute of Taisho University.

Takatsugu Hayashi specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Delhi and held posts at Tohoku University, Sendai National College of Technology, and Hosen Gakuen College.

Takayasu Higuchi was an archaeology, Central Asian, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University. He served as professor of archaeology at Kyoto University and director of the Archaeological Institute of Kashihara and Sen-oku Hakuko Kan.

Takayasu Kimura is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who completed doctoral studies at Taisho University. He worked as a research assistant at the University of Tokyo, a lecturer at Taisho University, and a researcher at the Shingon Buddhism Buzan-ha institute.
Takayasu Suzuki is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He served as a professor at Yamaguchi Prefectural University.

Takayoshi Kamei was a history/archaeology and Japanology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (1928–1947), Ibaraki University (1950–1961), and Seisen University (1961–1971).

Takayoshi Namikawa is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who completed his undergraduate and doctoral studies at Bukkyo University. He served as a professor and later emeritus professor at Bukkyo University, with additional visiting posts at Jawaharlal Nehru and Hokkaido universities.
Takayuki Hirosawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He served as a researcher and professor at Taisho University.
